reference: This corpus was written from SPEC-tieinoutageplanner.md revision 2026-10-17.4 (model 2026-10-09.to-3) without access to the page code; expectations were computed by the independent ref_impl.py and re-checked by the separately written verify.py (exact rational arithmetic, brute-force slot search, DFS cycle detection).

Kolisch, R. (1996). Efficient priority rules for the resource-constrained project scheduling problem. Journal of Operations Management 14(3), 179-192. (LST, LFT, MSLK, MTS, GRPW, SPT priority rules)

tolerance: numbers within 1e-9 x max(1,|expected|); arrays element by element with equal length; everything else (strings, booleans, null, object keys given) exact
not_benchmarked: decision_fingerprint hash value and its algorithm (cases use approve:true or a fingerprint assumed to differ)
the restored_values warning: warnings are omitted from expected in every case whose input triggers a section 10 replacement (marked restore_replaces:true)
text conversion of arrays/objects in text fields (JavaScript String() semantics)
status values with surrounding white space (exact vocabulary match vs trimming)
empty parts inside interval text (e.g. a trailing ';' or ';;')
generated ids colliding with explicit ids (e.g. an explicit 'task-2' and an id-less second row)

the blocking reason priority_rule_unsupported: every corpus input passes through section 10, which restores an out-of-vocabulary priority_rule to lst before validation (case pr-unsupported-unreachable-blocking-order); verify.py checks its position by a direct route
UI text, localisation, PDF report, Python export, project-package records
decision outputs in non-decision groups (only the decision group lists decision_approved/decision_stale)
